title: רב אחא בריה דרבא
author: Heilprin source tradition; Warsaw digital witness

paragraphs: Rav Acha, son of Rava, “in the name of received teaching.” Rashi: he received from his master, his master from his master, back to Rabbi Meir; he heard it on that authority, not his own explanation of Rabbi Meir’s reason, Yoma 33. Kiddushin 53, end of a: Rashi says it was familiar to the study hall’s members. He spoke to Rav Ashi: Berakhot 6, end of a; Yoma 32b; Shabbat 93b, 146a; Eruvin 43a, 77b; Yoma 25b; Shabbat 27b, 38b, and end of Hamotzi Yayin; Bava Kamma 47a, 62a; Menachot 38, end of b. Before Rav Ashi, Avodah Zarah 33a. Amemar, Mar Zutra, and Rav Ashi sat at a meal, with Rav Acha bar Rava attending, Arvei Pesachim 103b. He sat with Ravina before Rav Ashi, who gave him a knife to inspect. He inspected it; Rav Ashi said, “Well done,” Chullin 17b. In Rav Yehudah’s name, Yoma 53b; Ta'anit 24b. He sought two-and-one, since it came from Rav Kahana’s mouth, Sukkah 32, end of b. In Rav Yosef’s name, Pesachim 29, end of a. Ravina spoke to him, Pesachim 39a; “Does the master teach anything?”, Kol Gaggot 93b. He told Ravina that Amemar came to their locality and expounded. Yesh Nochalin 124b reads son of Rav—an error. Tosafot, Shabbat 93a, say Amemar was much later than Rava (see there); how could the early Rav Acha bar Rav tell the early Ravina about Amemar’s visit? The new editions did not correct it. Rav Acha son of Rava in Rabbi Yannai’s name, Zevachim 11b—requires examination; perhaps son of Rav, the earlier man, should be read. He said in Rav Bibi bar Abaye’s name, Shabbat 4a. Mar, his son; he and Rav Shmuel of Difti disagree. Eruvin 90b: Rav Acha son of Rav; Amsterdam’s edition has son of Rava. Perhaps it is the preceding Rav Acha bar Rav. Yuchasin takes unqualified Rav Acha with Ravina as this man. But see Rav Acha bar Rav: that man is the unqualified Rav Acha with Ravina, both early. See part I: he became head in 4170, for two years.
